rmt-2006-calc-01.title: Differentiate, then L'Hopital
rmt-2006-calc-01.body:
$\frac d{dx}\frac{\sin x}x=\frac{x\cos x-\sin x}{x^2}$, so the limit is $\lim_{x\to0}\frac{x\cos x-\sin x}{x^3}$. By L'Hopital: $\frac{\cos x-x\sin x-\cos x}{3x^2}=\frac{-x\sin x}{3x^2}=-\frac{\sin x}{3x}\to-\frac13$.

**Answer: $-\frac13$**

rmt-2006-calc-01.title: Taylor series
rmt-2006-calc-01.body:
$\frac{\sin x}x=1-\frac{x^2}6+\frac{x^4}{120}-\dots$, so $\frac d{dx}\frac{\sin x}x=-\frac x3+\frac{x^3}{30}-\dots$, and dividing by $x$ and letting $x\to0$ gives $-\frac13$.

**Answer: $-\frac13$**

rmt-2006-calc-02.title: Characteristic equation
rmt-2006-calc-02.body:
Substituting $y=e^{\lambda t}$ gives $(4\lambda^2+3\lambda-1)e^{\lambda t}=0$, so $4\lambda^2+3\lambda-1=(4\lambda-1)(\lambda+1)=0$, hence $\lambda=\frac14$ or $\lambda=-1$.

**Answer: $\lambda=\frac14,-1$**

rmt-2006-calc-06.title: Symmetry
rmt-2006-calc-06.body:
Substituting $x\to\frac\pi2-x$ shows $I=\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{\cos^3x}{\sin^3x+\cos^3x}dx$. Adding the two expressions, $2I=\int_0^{\pi/2}1\,dx=\frac\pi2$, so $I=\frac\pi4$.

**Answer: $\frac\pi4$**

rmt-2006-calc-07.title: Differentiate once more
rmt-2006-calc-07.body:
$H_{n+1}=(-1)^{n+1}e^{x^2}\frac{d^{n+1}}{dx^{n+1}}e^{-x^2}=-e^{x^2}\frac d{dx}\left[(-1)^n\frac{d^n}{dx^n}e^{-x^2}\right]=-e^{x^2}\frac d{dx}\left(e^{-x^2}H_n\right)$. By the product rule, $\frac d{dx}\left(e^{-x^2}H_n\right)=e^{-x^2}\left(-2xH_n+H_n'\right)$, so $H_{n+1}=2xH_n-H_n'$.

**Answer: $H_{n+1}=2xH_n-H_n'$**

rmt-2006-calc-08.title: Reduce to a horizontal rope
rmt-2006-calc-08.body:
The rope runs from the ground up to height 8 and has length 10, so its horizontal shadow has length $\sqrt{10^2-8^2}=6$. We can work with a horizontal rope of length 6 attached to the rim of the tower. At the start the unicorn is as far as possible from the center: the rope is radial.

*Phase 1.* The unicorn runs perpendicular to the rope, sweeping a quarter disk of radius 6 around the attachment point until the rope is tangent to the tower. Area $\frac14\pi6^2=9\pi$.

*Phase 2.* Now the rope winds onto the tower. When it has wound through angle $\theta$ (arc length $2\theta$), the free part is a tangent segment of length $L=6-2\theta$, $0\le\theta\le3$. Its tangent point moves along the segment's own direction, so it sweeps area only by rotating about the tangent point: $dA=\frac12L^2d\theta$. Total $\int_0^3\frac12(6-2\theta)^2d\theta=\frac12\left[36\theta-12\theta^2+\frac43\theta^3\right]_0^3=\frac12(108-108+36)=18$.

The two regions do not overlap, so the area is $18+9\pi$.

**Answer: $18+9\pi$**

rmt-2006-calc-09.title: Derivative of the inverse
rmt-2006-calc-09.body:
If $y=\tanh x$ then $x=\tanh^{-1}y=\frac12\ln\frac{1+y}{1-y}$, with derivative $\frac1{1-y^2}$. So $\frac d{dx}\tanh^{-1}(\tan x)=\frac{\sec^2x}{1-\tan^2x}=\frac{1/\cos^2x}{(\cos^2x-\sin^2x)/\cos^2x}=\frac1{\cos2x}=\sec2x$.

**Answer: $\sec2x$**

rmt-2006-calc-10.title: Use symmetry
rmt-2006-calc-10.body:
By the 4-fold symmetry about the center of the square, when Alan is at $(x,y)$ Bill is at $(1-y,x)$ (Alan's position rotated by $90^\circ$ about $(\frac12,\frac12)$). Alan moves toward Bill, so his velocity is parallel to $(1-y-x,\ x-y)$ and $\frac{dx}{dy}=\frac{1-x-y}{x-y}$ (the slope $\frac{dy}{dx}$ is infinite at $(0.6,0.4)$, so use $x$ as a function of $y$; the formula for $R$ is the same with the roles of $x,y$ exchanged).

At $(0.6,0.4)$: $\frac{dx}{dy}=\frac{0}{0.2}=0$. Differentiating with respect to $y$ (with $x'=\frac{dx}{dy}$): $x''=\frac{(-x'-1)(x-y)-(1-x-y)(x'-1)}{(x-y)^2}=\frac{(-1)(0.2)-0}{0.04}=-5$. Therefore $R=\frac{(1+0)^{3/2}}{|-5|}=\frac15$.

**Answer: $\frac15$**
